mcqs.question: What's the right way to decide R and W for a quorum system?
options: Always set R=1 and W=1 regardless of workload, since it's fastest
Pick R and W relative to N based on which side of the workload needs to be fast versus safe
Set R=N and W=N always to maximize safety, regardless of latency cost
Randomize R and W to average out the trade-off over time
mcqs.explanation: Quorum tuning is a deliberate trade-off against the actual workload shape, not a fixed setting. R=1/W=1 sacrifices safety for latency unconditionally; R=N/W=N sacrifices latency and fault tolerance unconditionally; randomizing gives up predictability entirely.

mcqs.question: For N=3, which split is write-optimized, trading slower reads for faster writes?
mcqs.explanation: W=1 means only one replica has to acknowledge a write before it returns, making writes fast; R=3 means every replica must respond to a read, making reads slow. W=3/R=1 is the opposite (read-optimized), and W=2/R=2 is the balanced middle.

mcqs.question: What do you give up by choosing the balanced R=2/W=2 split over a lopsided one?
options: Fault tolerance against any node failure
The ability to ever achieve strong consistency
The best-case latency either side could have alone — both sides end up middling instead
Nothing — it's strictly better than any lopsided split
mcqs.explanation: Balance is a trade, not a free win: R=2/W=2 avoids the worst-case latency of a lopsided split but also gives up the best-case latency either side could reach alone. Fault tolerance and strong-consistency capability aren't affected by this specific choice.

mcqs.question: What silently breaks when you set R+W=N instead of R+W>N?
options: The system stops accepting writes entirely
The read and write quorums are no longer guaranteed to share a replica, so a read can return stale data with no failures involved
The cluster can no longer tolerate any node failure
mcqs.explanation: R+W>N is exactly what guarantees the read and write quorums overlap on at least one replica; drop to R+W=N and that overlap is no longer guaranteed, so a read can miss the latest write even with every node healthy. Writes still succeed, replication still runs, and failure tolerance is a separate property from this overlap guarantee.
